top.line: A book can be an ordered set of articles
top.para: Ten Leanpub books stalled between 60% and 95%, and three agent-written graphs books are still under review two months on, because a book is one big batch. Articles are finished, linked and read daily. The hypothesis: books are curated articles plus an editorial thread, tested with four books for Web Summit, Lisbon, 9 to 12 November.

in-short.line: Books stall as batches; finished articles can become books
in-short.para: My books stall at 60 to 95%, ten on Leanpub and three on graphs.sgit.ai, because of the batch: one version, one review, one person. Articles do not stall. A book is an ordered set of finished articles plus the editorial thread, tested at Web Summit, and later used for other people's stories.

behind.line: Books stall because one big batch locks the content
behind.para: Leanpub lists ten unfinished books, such as Hacking Portugal at 95% since December 2016 and SecDevOps Risk Workflow at 64%. Three graphs books written in a day in August remain at v0.3.0, v0.2.0 and v0.1.0. The first version locks the content, review piles on one person, and energy moves on.

articles.line: Articles succeed because each is finished, linked and reviewed
articles.para: Each article goes from voice memo to research, figures and release on the same day, links instead of repeating, and gets feedback within days. Of the three graphs books, the one on how books were made read far better, written over 41 narrated releases and 38 verbatim briefs. Authentic source material makes better books.

hypothesis.line: Enough published articles can become a book straight away
hypothesis.para: If enough articles carry a book's key concepts and flows, a book is their curated order plus the editorial thread: introduction, order, transitions and index, which is my part as editor. The right number of articles and remaining editing are unknown. Books matter for revenue, learning, reach and finding adopters.

material.line: Enough material already exists for four candidate books
material.para: Approximate counts: Agents with a mandate has about 32 articles and 113,000 words, enough for one or two books; Graphs has about 12 articles and 54,000 words; Hacking Portugal about 8 articles and 25,000 words plus new talk articles for 2010, 2016, 2024 and 2025; and a book on making books.

plan.line: Map, write, assemble and publish on KDP by November
plan.para: Targets: map books by 19 October, write missing articles by 23, assemble a 6×9 PDF by 26, publish on Amazon KDP by 30, which may take up to 6 days for new accounts. Author copies come at print cost from Amazon.es, about €3.15 for 200 pages; a Lisbon printer is the fallback.

others.line: Later, the workflow could capture other people's untold stories
others.para: Constraints and failures are what stories lack, and people like rUv, with 226 public repositories, or Simon Wardley hold many uncaptured stories. The workflow could make books from them, but should improve first rather than experiment on someone else. As with the wires, the third or fifth book may be the one that hits.

limits.line: The hypothesis is untested and the dates are targets
limits.para: The first book is the test of the hypothesis. The dates are targets, and Amazon gives no delivery time for author copies. Article counts were made by hand from titles and tags, and the flight notes are mine; the graphs site records only a bunch of notes.

sources.line: Sources: Leanpub, graphs.sgit.ai, Amazon KDP and Web Summit
sources.para: Written by the site's agent from my voice memo of 16 October 2026. Sources are my Leanpub page and Hacking Portugal, graphs.sgit.ai's books, memos 39 and 44 and v0.5 release history, Amazon KDP help pages on publishing times, author copies and printing costs, Web Summit, and rUv's GitHub profile.
